title: AI Product Photo Generator for Sellers | AIVideosUGC
description: Turn one product photo into a listing image, a room scene, and an ad for your store. Skip the studio booking and see the cost before you start.
h1: Make listing, lifestyle, and ad images with an AI product photo generator
lead: A scene that felt like too much rigging can still be the photo. Describe the room you wanted for the candle, and the product you already shot goes there.

benefits.d: A studio day is the expensive part. Here each photo is 24 credits, so what you used to pay the photographer can go toward reaching buyers instead.

benefits.t: Create Photos Without a Studio Booking
benefits.d: The spring candle can go live from the photo you took on the packing table. A rental day does not have to be on the books first.

benefits.t: Create Several Scenes From One Upload
benefits.d: The same mug can be a white-background listing, a kitchen counter, and a square for an ad. A store can also send files through the API.

benefits.t: Skip the Model and Prop Rental
benefits.d: A ceramic vase does not need a hired model or a rented plant. Describe the shelf it sits on. If a hand should hold it, pick an AI actor.

benefits.t: Create Product Photos on Your Schedule
benefits.d: A holiday offer can be pictured on a Sunday night from the laptop. The tool does not keep studio hours.
Run the lotion on marble, then again on a bathroom shelf, and keep the one that matches the page.

faq.q: What can this product photo tool create?
faq.a: This tool creates a file you can put on a product page. Bring the photo you already have, and it builds a scene around the item.

faq.q: What do I upload to make a product photo?
faq.a: The clearest picture you have of the product, plus a sentence about where it should sit. A skillet reads better from a top-down photo than from a dark crop. Ask for a warmer light if the first file looks cold.

faq.q: What should a shop check before trusting a photo tool?
faq.a: Check that the product still matches what you sell. The file should keep the shape and color buyers recognize.

faq.q: What do I pay to start making photos?
faq.a: Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits. Each photo is 24 credits. Pro is $35 for 300 credits, and Premium is $63 for 600. You see the number before the photo is made.

faq.q: Can a shop put these photos on a product page?
faq.a: Yes. A three-candle set can use one file on the product page and another in an email. Check the glass color against the set you pack before either file goes out.

faq.q: Why make the photo here instead of reusing the supplier shot?
faq.a: It adds a scene to the supplier shot, such as a mug on a desk, while keeping the product recognizable.

faq.q: Am I allowed to post these photos on the store and in ads?
faq.a: Yes. The file downloads with no watermark. You still have to own the photo you started from, or have permission to use it. Our [AI product photography guide](page:blog-ai-product-photography-guide) covers that check.

faq.q: Can I put a price or a logo on the photo?
faq.a: Add prices, offers, and logo text in your own editor after download. Words drawn onto the photo can come out wrong, so proof them. See [Shopify product photos](page:plat-shopify) for where those files usually go.

faq.q: Where do I find product photo templates?
faq.a: Browse [product ad templates](page:templates) for plain product photos, lifestyle scenes, and ad layouts. Then upload your photo here and describe the scene.

faq.q: Can I make a stack of photos or connect my store?
faq.a: Yes. Upload several photos or send them from store software through the API, then make a scene for each.

faq.q: Can the photo become a video with a spoken line?
faq.a: Yes. Turn that photo into a product video, then add a spoken voice, on-screen captions, or a song from the music library. A 6-second clip uses 24 credits. A 10-second clip uses 40, a 15-second clip uses 60, and a 30-second clip uses 120. [Image to video](page:image-to-video) is that next step.

reviews.h2: Example Ways Shops Use the Photos
reviews.lead: These are example uses, not quotes from a named customer. Each card is one way a shop can continue from a product photo.

items.t: Turn the photo into a short product video
items.d: Start with the bottle photo. Turn it into a [product video](page:product-videos). Then add a spoken voice, on-screen captions, or a song from the music library.

items.t: Make the photo and the clip in one place
items.d: Upload the product photo and make the scene. Then trim the short video in the built-in editor, so you do not need another app.

items.t: Show a generated person holding the product
items.d: Use the photo so the product stays the same. A generated adult can hold it in a short video from [image to video](page:image-to-video).

items.t: Pick a generated actor for the clip
items.d: Choose a look from the [actor library](page:ai-actors), a set of generated people. Then keep the same person on the next version of the ad.

items.t: Make the same ad in more than one language
items.d: Write the script, then make the spoken version in the languages your shoppers use. Check the words before you publish.

items.t: See the credit cost before you start
items.d: Each photo runs on a paid plan, and the 24-credit charge shows before the job starts.

items.t: Use a generated presenter instead of a filming day
items.d: The actor is generated. Do not present the clip as a real customer or a celebrity.

items.t: Reuse one generated person from photos you have
items.d: Upload a few clear photos and reuse that generated person on the next scene. A presenter for the ad starts on [spokesperson videos](page:spokesperson-videos).

items.t: Start from a product link, then publish the ad
items.d: Paste a [product link](page:url-to-video) and the tool drafts a script. Then pick an actor and make a video. Publish that file to [TikTok](page:plat-tiktok) or [Facebook](page:plat-facebook) from the editor.

items.t: Ask for a script, a scene, and a clip
items.d: Describe the ad in chat. The tool drafts a script, a scene, and a short video you can trim in the editor.
